One-hundred four patients were randomized to transpulmonary pressure-guided ventilation group (n = 52) or lung rest strategy group (n = 52) groups.
This was a single-center prospective randomized controlled trial (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02439151).
Design: Single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial.

blinding.value: All nurses and other research personnel were blinded to the randomization schedule and block size. Data collectors were aware of the study group assignments, but the analyses were performed by a study statistician who did not participate in the study and did not know the research groupings. Because of the nature of the intervention, physicians and nurses could not be blinded to group assignments.

inclusion_criteria.value: 1) met the diagnostic criteria of Berlin definition for ARDS; 2) cause of ARDS was pneumonia; 3) had one of following disease-severity criteria despite optimum mechanical ventilation (tidal volume 6 mL/kg of predicted body weight, PEEP >= 10 cm H2O, FiO2 >= 0.8) and use of various rescue therapies: ratio of Pao2 to Fio2 less than or equal to 80 mm Hg; or an arterial blood pH less than 7.20 with a Paco2 greater than 60 mm Hg, with respiratory rate increased to 35 breaths per minute and Pplat less than or equal to 30 cm H2O.

provenance.quote: We included patients in whom a decision to initiate venovenous ECMO had already been made and met the following criteria: 1) met the diagnostic criteria of Berlin definition for ARDS (13); 2) cause of ARDS was pneumonia (Appendix S1, Supplemental Digital Content 1, http://links.lww.com/CCM/F572); and 3) had one of following disease-severity criteria despite optimum mechanical ventilation (tidal volume 6 mL/kg of predicted body weight [PBM], PEEP ≥ 10 cm H2O, Fio2 ≥ 0.8) and use of various rescue therapies: ratio of Pao2 to Fio2 less than or equal to 80 mm Hg; or an arterial blood pH less than 7.20 with a Paco2 greater than 60 mm Hg, with respiratory rate increased to 35 breaths per minute and Pplat less than or equal to 30 cm H2O.

exclusion_criteria.value: 1) age less than 18 years old; 2) patients had been on high pressure (Ppeak > 35 cm H2O) and high Fio2 greater than 0.8 ventilation for greater than 7 days; 3) patients already suffering pulmonary barotraumas; 4) had a contraindication to heparinization; 5) had an irreversible neurologic injury; or 6) severe chronic lung disease with life expectancy less than 6 months.

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ards_only: Berlin-defined ARDS was an inclusion criterion. obesity_subgroup: median BMI 24.1 kg/m2, obesity not an enrolment criterion. timing_subgroup: timing known only relative to randomisation/enrolment, so coded unclear per codebook ruling. ptp_target_subgroups: end-expiratory Ptp target 0-5 cm H2O via absolute Pes subtraction (Ptp = Paw - Pes implied by the Talmor approach the paper cites); the exact computation is in Appendix S2 which was not provided, so the absolute_pes_subtraction coding is flagged in unclear_items. is_longest_reported_mortality set on the 6-month mortality entry because 180 days outranks 60 days.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: No overlap with any cluster in COHORTS.md. Compared trial registration (NCT02439151, unique among listed clusters: EPVent-1 NCT00127491, EPVent-2, MGH NCT02503241/2015P001515), enrolment window (May 2015 to April 2019, single centre Beijing Chao-Yang Hospital, China), and population (severe ARDS on venovenous ECMO, pneumonia only). No other report in the candidate pool shares this registration, centre, or ECMO population.
unclear_items: intervention.balloon_calibration: no balloon, catheter brand, filling volume, or calibration method reported in the main text; details are in Appendix S2 (Supplemental Digital Content) which was not provided. Coded not_reported; contact author may be needed.

intervention.ptp_computation: the method for computing Ptp (absolute Pes subtraction vs elastance-derived) is not stated in the main text; coded absolute_pes_subtraction based on the cited Talmor approach, but Appendix S2 was not available to confirm.
intervention.device_brand: not reported in main text; likely in Appendix S2.
design.n_centers: single center stated but no numeric center count given; left null.
population.sex_female: paper reports only Male, n (%); female counts not reported and not derived.
outcomes: respiratory mechanics time-course numeric values are in Figure 2 and Supplemental Table S1 (not provided); only group-effect p-values from Figure 2 recorded.

arms[].peep_applied_cmh2o: delivered PEEP during ECMO reported only narratively ('PEEP was about 15 cm H2O in the Ptp-guided group') and in Figure 2/Table S1; no per-arm summary statistic with dispersion in the main text.
adults_18_plus: age exclusion <18 stated explicitly, so coded yes without inference.
data_only_in_figure: Time course of respiratory mechanics (PEEP, peak airway pressure, driving pressure, tidal volume, respiratory rate, mechanical power) at 2-120 hours, Figure 2 panels A-F
Cytokine levels (IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10) over time, Fig. S3 (supplement)
Lung density ratio post-ECMO/pre-ECMO by intercostal space, Fig. S4 (supplement)
extraction_flags.general_notes: Esophageal manometry details (device, calibration, Pes measurement) are confined to Appendix S2 of the supplemental digital content, which was not provided with this report; the main text establishes only that PEEP was titrated to end-expiratory Ptp 0-5 cm H2O. Two patients randomised to lung rest had cardiac arrest during ECMO establishment and were excluded from analysis (n analysed 52 vs 50). The paper reports 'Positive end-expiratory pressure (mm H2O)' in Table 3, an apparent typographical error for cm H2O; recorded with unit cm H2O as used elsewhere in the paper.
